initial_requirements: Military services need a common Tactical Control System for operating different current and future unmanned aerial vehicles and their payloads. Operators should be able to plan and control missions, monitor aircraft and payload status, receive and process sensor information, and distribute imagery and other mission products. The system must also exchange tasking and operational information with the wider command-and-control environment.

turns.interviewer_utterance:
Hello, I'm GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. Today, I’ll be gathering detailed information about the Tactical Control System to help ensure we understand the requirements clearly and completely.

Before we begin, are you in line with the scope of this interview, or do your expectations differ?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, I’m aligned with that scope. I’m here to help clarify what the Tactical Control System needs to do for mission planning, control, sensor handling, product distribution, and integration with the broader command-and-control environment.

turns.interviewer_utterance: To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I’m representing the operational side of the program, where we care about how the system will actually be used by operators and mission planners. My perspective is focused on making sure the system supports real UAV operations across different platforms and fits into existing command-and-control workflows.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Thank you. How would you describe this project in two to four sentences?
turns.interviewee_utterance: This project is to provide a common Tactical Control System that can operate current and future unmanned aerial vehicles and their payloads. It should let operators plan missions, monitor aircraft and payload status, handle sensor data, and distribute imagery and other mission products. It also needs to exchange tasking and operational information with the larger command-and-control environment.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Ok, now that I know the general goal, let's talk a bit about the systems and workflows you currently use. Can you describe the current process or system you use for planning and controlling UAV missions?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Right now, mission planning and control are usually handled with a mix of platform-specific ground control stations and manual coordination with the operations center. That means the workflow can differ depending on the UAV, and operators often have to translate tasking information between systems. It works, but it’s slow and creates a lot of opportunities for inconsistency when we switch between aircraft or pass information to other command-and-control tools.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what main features do you hope to get from this Tactical Control System?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We want to reduce the fragmentation between different UAV systems so operators can use one common workflow instead of relearning each platform. The main things we need are mission planning, real-time control and status monitoring, sensor and imagery handling, and clean exchange of tasking and mission products with other command-and-control systems. We also want to cut down on manual re-entry and make it easier to move from planning to execution without losing information.

turns.interviewer_utterance: So the main features/functions you want are: a common workflow across UAV platforms, mission planning, real-time control and status monitoring, sensor and imagery handling, exchange of tasking and mission products with other command-and-control systems, and reduced manual re-entry between planning and execution. Is that correct?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that’s correct. That captures the core of what we’re trying to achieve.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?
turns.interviewee_utterance: One thing that would be valuable is better traceability and auditability so we can see what was tasked, what was actually flown, and what products were produced. It would also help if the system supported role-based access and different levels of control, since not every user should be able to do everything. If those are already implied, then the next big need would be smooth interoperability with whatever legacy systems we still have to keep in the loop.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Based on your description, do you think role-based access control and audit/traceability should also be included?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, I think both should be included. They’re not just nice-to-have features; they’re important for security, accountability, and operational oversight.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We’d probably want strong messaging and collaboration support for operators and mission planners, especially when the aircraft is being retasked or the situation changes quickly. It would also be useful to have configurable alerts or notifications for key status changes and mission events. Beyond that, I’d want to make sure the system is resilient and can keep operating even when communications are degraded.

turns.interviewer_utterance: So these features/functions are desired: common workflow across UAV platforms, mission planning, real-time control and status monitoring, sensor and imagery handling, exchange of tasking and mission products with other command-and-control systems, reduced manual re-entry, role-based access control, auditability/traceability, interoperability with legacy systems, messaging and collaboration support, configurable alerts/notifications, and resilience during degraded communications. Is that correct?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that’s correct. Those all fit with what we’d want from the Tactical Control System.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which of these features should be considered the highest priority for the first release?
turns.interviewee_utterance: For the first release, I’d prioritize mission planning, real-time control and status monitoring, and the exchange of tasking and mission products with the wider command-and-control environment. After that, role-based access, auditability, and reduced manual re-entry should come next because they’re important for safe and efficient operations. The messaging, alerts, and resilience features are also important, but I’d see them as secondary to getting the core operational workflow working first.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want mission planning to accomplish in this Tactical Control System.
turns.interviewee_utterance: Mission planning should let operators define the UAV mission from start to finish in a way that is quick and accurate. That means setting routes, targets, timing, payload use, and tasking details in a format that can be carried through to execution without having to re-enter everything manually. It should also support updates when the mission changes, so planners can adjust and push those changes cleanly to the aircraft and payloads.

turns.interviewer_utterance: How would you like mission planning updates to be applied when a mission changes: should they overwrite the existing plan automatically, require operator approval, or follow a different process?
turns.interviewee_utterance: They should require operator approval before anything is applied. Automatic overwriting would be too risky in an operational setting, especially if the change affects routing, payload use, or tasking already in motion. I’d want the system to show the proposed update clearly, let the operator review it, and then confirm before it becomes the active plan.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want real-time control and status monitoring to accomplish in this Tactical Control System.
turns.interviewee_utterance: It should give operators a current picture of each UAV’s position, flight state, payload state, and mission progress without lag that would affect decisions. They need to be able to see whether the aircraft is healthy, whether the sensor is working, and whether the mission is still executing as planned. It should also support sending control inputs when needed, like changing a mission parameter or redirecting the aircraft, with immediate feedback that the command was received and acted on.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What level of immediacy or latency is acceptable for those status updates and command acknowledgements?
turns.interviewee_utterance: For status updates, we’d want them to feel near real-time, ideally within a couple of seconds under normal conditions. Command acknowledgements should come back as quickly as possible, also within a few seconds, so the operator knows the system accepted the action. If communications are degraded, it can be slower, but the system should clearly show that the link is delayed rather than leaving the operator guessing.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want the exchange of tasking and mission products with the wider command-and-control environment to accomplish.
turns.interviewee_utterance: It should let the Tactical Control System send and receive tasking, mission updates, imagery, and other products to and from external command-and-control systems without manual translation. The goal is to keep the UAV operators aligned with the broader operational picture and make sure higher headquarters or other units can consume the products quickly. It also needs to reduce duplicate data entry and preserve the structure of the information as much as possible across systems.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which external command-and-control systems or interfaces must this Tactical Control System integrate with first?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The first priority is whatever command-and-control systems are already in operational use by the services, but I can’t name a single one with confidence without checking the integration list. In practice, we’d want to start with the systems that handle tasking, situation awareness, and product dissemination most often. If there are mandated tactical data links or common message standards in the environment, those would need to be included early as well.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you list the specific message standards, tactical data links, or interface types that must be supported first, or should I treat that as an integration requirement to be confirmed later?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Treat that as an integration requirement to be confirmed later. I know we’ll need compatibility with whatever standards and links are already mandated in the operational environment, but I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong set. Once the integration stakeholders review it, we can pin down the specific message formats and interfaces that have to be supported first.

turns.interviewer_utterance: How would you like role-based access control to be defined for the main user groups in this system?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Role-based access should be tied to operational duties rather than just generic user labels. For example, an operator should control missions and payloads, a supervisor should review and approve higher-risk actions, and an analyst or recipient might only view and distribute mission products. We’d also want administrator access separated so system setup and security functions are not mixed with day-to-day mission operations.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want auditability and traceability to accomplish in this Tactical Control System.
turns.interviewee_utterance: We need to be able to reconstruct who did what, when, and from where for mission actions, control inputs, and product dissemination. That means every significant event should be logged in a way that supports operational review, incident investigation, and accountability. It should also help us trace a mission product back to the source data and the sequence of actions that led to it.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What level of detail should those audit logs capture for mission actions and product dissemination?
turns.interviewee_utterance: They should capture enough detail to recreate the decision and action path without becoming unusably noisy. For mission actions, that means the user, time, aircraft or payload involved, the command issued, the result, and any acknowledgement or failure. For dissemination, it should record what product was sent, to whom or to what system, when it was released, and whether delivery succeeded.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Please elaborate on what you want reduced manual re-entry to accomplish in this Tactical Control System.
turns.interviewee_utterance: The idea is to avoid operators having to type the same mission details, aircraft status, or product metadata into multiple systems. If information is already captured in the Tactical Control System, we want it to flow into downstream reports, tasking updates, and external systems as automatically as possible. That should save time, reduce transcription errors, and keep the operational picture consistent.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What other stakeholders do you think have valuable insights into this project, and whose needs should be considered, and why?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The most important additional stakeholders are the operators, mission supervisors, intelligence or imagery analysts, and the command staff who consume the products and tasking updates. We also need the communications and integration teams, because they understand the external systems and constraints, and the cyber or security team for access, logging, and accreditation concerns. Finally, maintenance or platform support personnel matter if they need health status, fault reporting, or configuration access that affects readiness.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What do you consider a successful deployment of this Tactical Control System?
turns.interviewee_utterance: A successful deployment means operators can use one system to plan, control, and monitor missions across the supported unmanned aircraft without losing situational awareness or relying on workarounds. It should exchange the right data with the broader command-and-control environment, and it should do so reliably enough that users trust it in real operations. I’d also consider it successful if it reduces manual effort and errors, and if the transition into use does not disrupt ongoing missions.

turns.interviewer_utterance: To summarize, we discussed a Tactical Control System that provides a common workflow across UAV platforms; mission planning with operator-approved updates; real-time control and near-real-time status monitoring; exchange of tasking, imagery, and mission products with external command-and-control systems; role-based access control; auditability and traceability; reduced manual re-entry; messaging/collaboration; alerts/notifications; and resilience in degraded communications. Is there anything else you would like to add?
turns.interviewee_utterance: That summary is broadly right. I’d just add that the system should be flexible enough to accommodate new UAV platforms and payloads over time without a major redesign, and it should support secure operation in disconnected or intermittent network conditions. If those are built in from the start, it will be much easier to keep the system useful as missions and integration needs evolve.
